Material colors are the Okabe–Ito palette, matched to the requested hues: rock/stone green, granite pink, metal brown, marble dark yellow, others blue. Pale yellow is not used, because it disappears on white, and a darker gold than `#E69F00` starts to collide with the other fills for tritanopia. Checked with `colorspace` simulations of deuteranopia, protanopia, and tritanopia. Minimum CIE Lab distance: normal vision 41, deuteranopia 18, protanopia 23, tritanopia 17.

Every later figure uses these same colors. A focal monument–material group takes the color of its material: Brazil — granite is pink, Israel — others is blue, Israel — rock/stone is green, United States — marble is dark yellow, and United States — metal is brown.

Charging Bull and Fearless Girl are both inside the US metal group, so the metal brown cannot separate them. Pure red is not a color-blind-safe color: under deuteranopia it collapses toward brown and green. The safe red in the Okabe–Ito palette is vermillion `#D55E00`. Fearless Girl uses the IBM color-blind purple `#785EF0`, which stays far from that red. Distance between them: normal vision 134, deuteranopia 134, protanopia 125, tritanopia 91.

```{r helpers}
clean_sample_id <- function(x) {
  x <- basename(as.character(x))
  x <- str_remove(x, "\\.(fastq|fq)(\\.gz)?$")
  x <- str_remove(x, "_R[12](_001)?$")
  x <- str_remove(x, "_S[0-9]+.*$")
  x
}

normalize_material <- function(x) {
  x <- str_to_lower(str_squish(as.character(x)))
  case_when(
    is.na(x) | x == "" ~ "Unknown",
    x %in% c("rock", "stone", "rock/stone") ~ "rock/stone",
    x == "granite" ~ "granite",
    x == "marble" ~ "marble",
    x %in% c("metal", "bronze", "steel", "gold") ~ "metal",
    x %in% c("other", "others") ~ "others",
    TRUE ~ "others"
  )
}

# Figure theme, Jaccard NMDS, Mann-Whitney brackets, and PNG/PDF savers.
FIG_FONT <- "Helvetica"
PRINT_WIDTH_IN <- 180 / 25.4     # 7.09 in, the maximum width allowed
PRINT_MAX_HEIGHT_IN <- 10.6      # A4 is 11.69 in; leaves room for a page margin
PRINT_DPI <- 600
CHECK_DPI <- 300

set_figure_mode <- function(mode = c("check", "print")) {
  mode <- match.arg(mode)
  sizes <- switch(
    mode,
    check = list(
      FIG_BASE_SIZE = 15, FIG_TITLE_SIZE = 17, FIG_AXIS_TITLE_SIZE = 16,
      FIG_LEGEND_TEXT_SIZE = 13, FIG_LEGEND_TITLE_SIZE = 14, FIG_TAG_SIZE = 24,
      FIG_SMALL_TEXT_SIZE = 12, FIG_GEOM = 1
    ),
    print = list(
      FIG_BASE_SIZE = 7, FIG_TITLE_SIZE = 7, FIG_AXIS_TITLE_SIZE = 7,
      FIG_LEGEND_TEXT_SIZE = 6, FIG_LEGEND_TITLE_SIZE = 7, FIG_TAG_SIZE = 8,
      FIG_SMALL_TEXT_SIZE = 6, FIG_GEOM = 0.45
    )
  )
  assign("FIG_MODE", mode, envir = globalenv())
  for (nm in names(sizes)) assign(nm, sizes[[nm]], envir = globalenv())
  invisible(mode)
}
set_figure_mode("check")

is_print <- function() identical(FIG_MODE, "print")
pt_to_mm <- function(pt) pt / ggplot2::.pt
gs <- function(x) x * FIG_GEOM          # point sizes and line widths
# In print mode every size that is written in inches for the check figures is scaled down
# by the same ratio as the text (7 pt / 15 pt).
fs <- function(x) x * FIG_BASE_SIZE / 15
# Choose a value by mode.
by_mode <- function(check, print) if (is_print()) print else check

# Axis titles sit a few points from the tick labels, never far away.
paper_theme <- function(base_size = FIG_BASE_SIZE, angle_x = TRUE) {
  m <- base_size / 15   # margins scale with the text
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size, base_family = FIG_FONT) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = FIG_TITLE_SIZE, margin = margin(t = 10 * m, b = 6 * m)),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = base_size, margin = margin(b = 4 * m)),
      plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = FIG_TAG_SIZE),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = FIG_AXIS_TITLE_SIZE, margin = margin(t = 5 * m)),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = FIG_AXIS_TITLE_SIZE, margin = margin(r = 5 * m)),
      axis.text = element_text(size = base_size, colour = "black"),
      axis.text.x = if (angle_x) {
        element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, colour = "black")
      } else {
        element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, lineheight = 0.95, colour = "black")
      },
      axis.ticks.length = unit(4 * m, "pt"),
      axis.line = element_line(linewidth = gs(0.5)),
      axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = gs(0.5)),
      legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = FIG_LEGEND_TITLE_SIZE),
      legend.text = element_text(size = FIG_LEGEND_TEXT_SIZE),
      legend.key.size = unit(0.55 * m, "cm"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = base_size),
      plot.margin = margin(8 * m, 14 * m, 8 * m, 8 * m)
    )
}

paper_theme_continuous <- function(base_size = FIG_BASE_SIZE) {
  paper_theme(base_size, angle_x = FALSE)
}

# Theme for panels with many categorical tick labels that stay upright.
paper_theme_upright <- function(base_size = FIG_BASE_SIZE) {
  paper_theme(base_size, angle_x = FALSE)
}

# Blank theme for Venn diagrams, with the same text sizes.
venn_theme <- function() {
  theme_void(base_size = FIG_BASE_SIZE, base_family = FIG_FONT) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = FIG_TITLE_SIZE),
      plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = FIG_TAG_SIZE),
      legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = FIG_LEGEND_TITLE_SIZE),
      legend.text = element_text(size = FIG_LEGEND_TEXT_SIZE),
      legend.key.height = unit(by_mode(0.8, 0.35), "cm"),
      legend.key.width = unit(by_mode(0.5, 0.25), "cm"),
      plot.margin = margin(by_mode(8, 3), by_mode(14, 5), by_mode(8, 3), by_mode(8, 3))
    )
}

# Axis, legend, and title text. Accented names are kept in the metadata and
# reduced here, because the figure device prints a missing glyph as <U+XXXX>.
plot_label <- function(x) {
  y <- as.character(x)
  ok <- !is.na(y)
  y[ok] <- stringi::stri_trans_general(y[ok], "Latin-ASCII")
  y[ok] <- str_replace_all(y[ok], "\u00b2", "2")
  y[ok] <- str_replace_all(y[ok], "\u00b3", "3")
  bad <- y[ok & grepl("[^\x01-\x7F]", y)]
  if (length(bad) > 0) {
    stop("A plot label still contains a character the figure device cannot draw: ", paste(unique(bad), collapse = " | "))
  }
  y
}

figure_text <- function(x, depth = 0L) {
  if (is.null(x) || depth > 40L) return(character())
  if (inherits(x, "ggplot")) x <- ggplotGrob(x)
  out <- character()
  lab <- x$label
  if (is.expression(lab) || is.language(lab) || is.symbol(lab)) lab <- as.character(lab)
  if (is.character(lab)) out <- c(out, lab)
  if (!is.null(x$children)) out <- c(out, unlist(lapply(x$children, figure_text, depth + 1L), use.names = FALSE))
  if (!is.null(x$grobs)) out <- c(out, unlist(lapply(x$grobs, figure_text, depth + 1L), use.names = FALSE))
  out
}

save_figure <- function(filename, plot, ...) {
  labels <- figure_text(plot)
  bad <- labels[grepl("[^\x01-\x7F]|<U\\+", labels)]
  if (length(bad) > 0) {
    stop("Figure text is not plain ASCII:\n", paste(unique(bad), collapse = "\n"))
  }
  ggsave(filename, plot, ...)
}

# Check mode: save one panel as a PNG inside the figure's own folder. In print mode this
# does nothing, so the same chunk can be run in both modes. Returns the path or NULL.
save_panel <- function(plot, figure_dir, file_name, width, height, dpi = CHECK_DPI) {
  if (is_print()) return(invisible(NULL))
  dir.create(figure_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  path <- file.path(figure_dir, paste0(file_name, ".png"))
  save_figure(path, plot, width = width, height = height, units = "in", dpi = dpi, bg = "white")
  invisible(path)
}

# Each panel is wrapped as an independent block, so panels are not aligned to each other
# and no axis title is pushed away from its axis by a neighbour's tick labels.
blk <- function(p) patchwork::wrap_elements(full = p)

# vegan permutation tests report p = (d+1)/(N+1). With N = 999 the smallest value is
# 0.001, which means none of the permutations was as extreme as the observed statistic.
perm_p_text <- function(p, nperm = 999L) {
  p <- as.numeric(p)[[1]]
  floor_p <- 1 / (as.numeric(nperm)[[1]] + 1)
  if (is.finite(p) && p <= floor_p + 1e-12) {
    sprintf("p < %.3g", floor_p)
  } else {
    sprintf("p = %.3g", p)
  }
}

# Jaccard presence-absence distances, PERMANOVA, and 2-D NMDS. Taxa found in
# only one sample are dropped: they inflate Jaccard toward 1 and make 2-D NMDS
# degenerate. Samples that then have no remaining taxa are dropped from the
# distance matrix. NMDS has no percent-explained axes; stress is reported instead.
jaccard_beta <- function(mat, group, nperm = 999L, seed = 123L, trymax = 200L, min_occupancy = 2L) {
  if (is.null(rownames(mat))) rownames(mat) <- as.character(seq_len(nrow(mat)))
  pa <- (mat > 0) * 1
  storage.mode(pa) <- "numeric"
  rownames(pa) <- rownames(mat)
  if (min_occupancy > 1L && ncol(pa) > 0) {
    pa <- pa[, colSums(pa) >= min_occupancy, drop = FALSE]
  }
  keep <- rowSums(pa) > 0
  dropped_samples <- rownames(pa)[!keep]
  pa <- pa[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  group <- group[keep]
  d <- vegan::vegdist(pa, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)
  grp <- data.frame(focal_group = group)
  set.seed(seed)
  permanova <- vegan::adonis2(d ~ focal_group, data = grp, permutations = nperm)
  set.seed(seed)
  nmds <- vegan::metaMDS(d, k = 2, trymax = trymax, trace = FALSE)
  scores <- as.data.frame(vegan::scores(nmds, display = "sites"))
  names(scores) <- c("NMDS1", "NMDS2")
  rownames(scores) <- rownames(pa)
  list(
    dist = d, permanova = permanova, nmds = nmds, scores = scores, stress = nmds$stress,
    dropped_samples = dropped_samples, n_samples = nrow(pa), n_taxa = ncol(pa)
  )
}

# Pairwise Mann-Whitney (Wilcoxon) tests with BH adjustment.
pairwise_mannwhitney <- function(x, g, p_adjust = "BH") {
  g <- droplevels(factor(g))
  lv <- levels(g)
  if (length(lv) < 2) {
    return(data.frame(group1 = character(), group2 = character(), p_raw = double(), p_adj = double(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  }
  group1 <- character()
  group2 <- character()
  p_raw <- double()
  for (i in seq_len(length(lv) - 1L)) {
    for (j in (i + 1L):length(lv)) {
      xi <- x[g == lv[i] & is.finite(x)]
      xj <- x[g == lv[j] & is.finite(x)]
      p <- if (length(xi) < 2L || length(xj) < 2L) {
        NA_real_
      } else {
        stats::wilcox.test(xi, xj, exact = FALSE)$p.value
      }
      group1 <- c(group1, lv[i])
      group2 <- c(group2, lv[j])
      p_raw <- c(p_raw, p)
    }
  }
  data.frame(group1 = group1, group2 = group2, p_raw = p_raw, p_adj = stats::p.adjust(p_raw, method = p_adjust), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

mw_p_text <- function(p) {
  p <- as.numeric(p)[[1]]
  if (!is.finite(p)) return("")
  if (p < 0.001) "p < 0.001" else sprintf("p = %.3g", p)
}

# Square brackets for BH-significant pairwise Mann-Whitney tests.
mw_bracket_data <- function(y, group, pw) {
  sig <- pw[is.finite(pw$p_adj) & pw$p_adj < 0.05, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(sig)) return(sig)
  lv <- levels(droplevels(factor(group)))
  sig$i1 <- match(sig$group1, lv)
  sig$i2 <- match(sig$group2, lv)
  sig <- sig[order(sig$i2 - sig$i1, sig$i1), , drop = FALSE]
  ymax <- max(y[is.finite(y)], na.rm = TRUE)
  ymin <- min(y[is.finite(y)], na.rm = TRUE)
  rng <- ymax - ymin
  if (!is.finite(rng) || rng <= 0) rng <- max(abs(ymax), 1)
  sig$label <- vapply(sig$p_adj, mw_p_text, character(1))
  sig$y.position <- ymax + rng * 0.12 * seq_len(nrow(sig))
  sig
}

mw_kw_subtitle <- function(kw_p, pw) {
  sprintf("Kruskal-Wallis p = %.3g", kw_p)
}

# Print mode: save one A4-portrait page as PDF (vector) and PNG (600 dpi). In check mode
# this does nothing. The page must be at most 180 mm wide and must fit A4 portrait.
save_page <- function(plot, figure_dir, name, height, width = PRINT_WIDTH_IN) {
  if (!is_print()) return(invisible(NULL))
  if (width > PRINT_WIDTH_IN + 1e-6) stop(name, ": wider than 180 mm (", round(width * 25.4), " mm).")
  if (height > PRINT_MAX_HEIGHT_IN + 1e-6) stop(name, ": taller than the A4 page allows (", round(height, 2), " in).")
  dir.create(figure_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  pdf_path <- file.path(figure_dir, paste0(name, ".pdf"))
  png_path <- file.path(figure_dir, paste0(name, ".png"))
  save_figure(pdf_path, plot, width = width, height = height, units = "in", device = grDevices::pdf, family = FIG_FONT)
  save_figure(png_path, plot, width = width, height = height, units = "in", dpi = PRINT_DPI, bg = "white")
  invisible(png_path)
}

# Named genera from sheet 1 of the validated literature table. Cutibacterium is marked
# "NOT recommended" and is left out; the Bryobacter aside on the Blastocatella row is left out.
literature_genera_from_sheet <- function(path) {
  sheet <- readr::read_csv(path, skip = 1, show_col_types = FALSE)
  status <- sheet[["Validation status"]]
  status[is.na(status)] <- ""
  genus_cells <- sheet$Genus[!stringr::str_detect(status, stringr::regex("NOT recommended", ignore_case = TRUE))]
  parsed <- lapply(genus_cells, function(cell) {
    if (is.na(cell)) return(character())
    cell <- stringr::str_replace_all(cell, "[^A-Za-z0-9 ;/._-]", " ")
    cell <- stringr::str_replace(cell, stringr::regex("also deterioration-associated Bryobacter.*$", ignore_case = TRUE), "")
    cell <- stringr::str_replace_all(cell, stringr::regex("-type AOA", ignore_case = TRUE), "")
    if (stringr::str_detect(cell, stringr::regex("unresolved|copper-resistant", ignore_case = TRUE))) return(character())
    parts <- stringr::str_trim(unlist(stringr::str_split(cell, "[;/]")))
    parts <- parts[stringr::str_detect(parts, "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_.]*$|^Ca\\.")]
    unlist(lapply(parts, function(genus_name) {
      genus_name <- stringr::str_replace(genus_name, "^Ca\\.\\s*", "Candidatus_")
      genus_name <- stringr::str_replace_all(genus_name, " ", "_")
      if (genus_name == "Candidatus_Nitrocosmicus") {
        return(c("Candidatus_Nitrosocosmicus", "Nitrosocosmicus"))
      }
      if (genus_name == "Candidatus_Nitrosotenuis") return("Nitrosotenuis")
      genus_name
    }))
  })
  unique(unlist(parsed))
}

# Last token of a MetaPhlAn clade_name, as rank plus taxon. Used by Figure 3 and Figure 5.
parse_terminal_rank <- function(clade_name) {
  terminal <- str_extract(clade_name, "[^|]+$")
  prefix <- str_extract(terminal, "^[kpcofgst]__")
  rank <- recode(
    prefix,
    "p__" = "phylum",
    "g__" = "genus",
    "s__" = "species",
    .default = NA_character_
  )
  tibble(rank = rank, taxon = str_remove(terminal, "^[kpcofgst]__"))
}
```

Metadata come from `input/Monumentome_metadata.csv`, using `monument_final` and `materials_final`. Panel C keeps samples with at least 2 detected species, using the same focal-group rules as the analysis notebook.

The species table is not the raw MetaPhlAn output. `decontaminate_metaphlan.R` builds the noise list from the two positive standards whose profiles matched the ZymoBIOMICS mix, `BC-0247288828` (Soldier's National Monument) and `BC-0302366907` (Orpheus). A species in either of those two that is not one of the ten D6300 organisms is subtracted, at its higher abundance in the two, from every sample, and each sample is renormalised to 100. Two further samples had been typed as positive standards, `BC-0247292781` (Soldier's National Monument) and `BC-0302370816` (Seoul Tower). Their profiles did not match the mix, so those two rows were removed from the metadata. They are also left out of the transformed table. The script is run here so the table on disk always matches the raw table. The noise list and its effect are shown in `supplementary_figures.Rmd` under Supplementary Figure 1.

The two matched positive standards and all eleven negative controls are removed before any focal-group rule is applied. Both matched standards were logged against Soldier's National Monument or Orpheus with material marble, so without that step they would sit inside United States — marble. The three Tel Megiddo samples typed `control` are swabs of a touched rock surface and are kept.

```{r load-data}
metadata <- read_csv(METADATA_FILE, show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "unique") %>%
  mutate(
    sample_name_clean = clean_sample_id(sample_name),
    materials_plot = normalize_material(materials_final),
    monument_label = plot_label(str_replace_all(as.character(monument_final), "_", " "))
  )

QC_POSITIVE_CONTROLS <- c(
  "BC-0247288828",
  "BC-0302366907"
)
MISLABELED_SAMPLES <- c(
  "BC-0247292781",
  "BC-0302370816"
)

ZYMO_D6300_SPECIES <- c(
  "Pseudomonas_aeruginosa",
  "Escherichia_coli",
  "Salmonella_enterica",
  "Limosilactobacillus_fermentum",  # Zymo sheet: Lactobacillus fermentum
  "Enterococcus_faecalis",
  "Staphylococcus_aureus",
  "Listeria_monocytogenes",
  "Bacillus_spizizenii",            # Zymo sheet: Bacillus subtilis
  "Saccharomyces_cerevisiae",
  "Cryptococcus_neoformans"
)

decontaminate_metaphlan <- function(root = ".",
                                    metaphlan_file = file.path(root, "input", "metaphlan_merged_all_taxa.tsv"),
                                    metadata_file = file.path(root, "input", "Monumentome_metadata.csv"),
                                    noise_out = file.path(root, "input", "positive_control_noise_species.tsv"),
                                    table_out = file.path(root, "input", "metaphlan_merged_all_taxa_decontaminated.tsv"),
                                    positive_control_type = "positive_control",
                                    positive_control_ids = QC_POSITIVE_CONTROLS,
                                    zymo_species = ZYMO_D6300_SPECIES,
                                    quiet = FALSE) {
  strip_s_suffix <- function(x) str_remove(as.character(x), "_S[0-9]+.*$")

  header_lines <- readLines(metaphlan_file, n = 5)
  header_lines <- header_lines[str_starts(header_lines, "#")]

  mp <- read_tsv(metaphlan_file, comment = "#", show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "minimal")
  if ("#clade_name" %in% names(mp)) names(mp)[names(mp) == "#clade_name"] <- "clade_name"
  sample_cols <- setdiff(names(mp), c("clade_name", "NCBI_tax_id"))
  sample_ids <- strip_s_suffix(sample_cols)
  # Mislabeled positive controls are not part of the analysis table.
  drop_cols <- sample_cols[sample_ids %in% MISLABELED_SAMPLES]
  if (length(drop_cols) != length(MISLABELED_SAMPLES)) {
    stop("Mislabeled samples missing from the MetaPhlAn table: ",
         paste(setdiff(MISLABELED_SAMPLES, sample_ids), collapse = ", "))
  }
  sample_cols <- setdiff(sample_cols, drop_cols)
  sample_ids <- strip_s_suffix(sample_cols)

  metadata <- read_csv(metadata_file, show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "unique")
  metadata_ids <- unique(strip_s_suffix(metadata$sample_name))
  # Sample columns that are not in the metadata are not paper samples.
  sample_cols <- sample_cols[sample_ids %in% metadata_ids]
  sample_ids <- strip_s_suffix(sample_cols)
  typed_positive <- metadata %>%
    filter(sample_type == positive_control_type) %>%
    pull(sample_name) %>%
    strip_s_suffix()
  positive_ids <- strip_s_suffix(positive_control_ids)
  missing_ids <- setdiff(positive_ids, typed_positive)
  if (length(missing_ids) > 0) {
    stop("These QC positive controls are not typed ", positive_control_type, " in the metadata: ",
         paste(missing_ids, collapse = ", "))
  }
  positive_cols <- sample_cols[sample_ids %in% positive_ids]
  if (length(positive_cols) != length(positive_ids)) {
    stop("These QC positive controls have no MetaPhlAn column: ",
         paste(setdiff(positive_ids, sample_ids), collapse = ", "))
  }

  mat <- as.matrix(mp[, sample_cols])
  mode(mat) <- "numeric"
  mat[is.na(mat)] <- 0
  rownames(mat) <- mp$clade_name

  is_species_row <- str_detect(mp$clade_name, "\\|s__[^|]+$")
  species_name <- if_else(is_species_row, str_remove(str_extract(mp$clade_name, "[^|]+$"), "^s__"), NA_character_)

  # Noise list: species seen in a positive control that are not in the standard.
  pos_mat <- mat[is_species_row, positive_cols, drop = FALSE]
  rownames(pos_mat) <- species_name[is_species_row]
  seen <- rowSums(pos_mat > 0) > 0
  noise <- tibble(
    species = rownames(pos_mat)[seen],
    ceiling_abundance = apply(pos_mat[seen, , drop = FALSE], 1, max),
    n_positive_controls = rowSums(pos_mat[seen, , drop = FALSE] > 0),
    positive_controls = apply(pos_mat[seen, , drop = FALSE], 1, function(v) paste(strip_s_suffix(positive_cols)[v > 0], collapse = ";"))
  ) %>%
    filter(!species %in% zymo_species) %>%
    arrange(desc(ceiling_abundance))

  # Subtract each noise species, propagate, then renormalise.
  removed_total <- setNames(numeric(length(sample_cols)), sample_cols)
  samples_touched <- setNames(integer(nrow(noise)), noise$species)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(noise))) {
    sp <- noise$species[i]
    row_i <- which(is_species_row & species_name == sp)
    if (length(row_i) != 1) stop("Species row not unique: ", sp)
    lineage <- mp$clade_name[row_i]
    ancestors <- which(vapply(mp$clade_name, function(cn) cn != lineage & str_starts(lineage, fixed(paste0(cn, "|"))), logical(1)))
    children <- which(str_starts(mp$clade_name, fixed(paste0(lineage, "|"))))

    ab <- mat[row_i, ]
    removed <- pmin(ab, noise$ceiling_abundance[i])
    samples_touched[sp] <- sum(removed > 0)
    removed_total <- removed_total + removed

    mat[row_i, ] <- ab - removed
    for (a in ancestors) mat[a, ] <- mat[a, ] - removed
    if (length(children)) {
      scale <- ifelse(ab > 0, (ab - removed) / ab, 1)
      mat[children, ] <- sweep(mat[children, , drop = FALSE], 2, scale, "*")
    }
  }
  mat[mat < 1e-9] <- 0

  top_rows <- !str_detect(mp$clade_name, fixed("|"))
  totals <- colSums(mat[top_rows, , drop = FALSE])
  factor <- ifelse(totals > 0, 100 / totals, 1)
  mat <- sweep(mat, 2, factor, "*")
  mat <- round(mat, 6)

  out <- bind_cols(tibble(clade_name = mp$clade_name), as_tibble(mat))
  if ("NCBI_tax_id" %in% names(mp)) out <- bind_cols(out[, 1], mp["NCBI_tax_id"], out[, -1])

  dir.create(dirname(table_out), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  writeLines(
    c(header_lines,
      paste0("#decontaminated ", format(Sys.Date()), ": ", nrow(noise),
             " positive-control noise species subtracted at their ceiling, then renormalised to 100 per sample (decontaminate_metaphlan.R)")),
    table_out
  )
  write_tsv(out, table_out, append = TRUE, col_names = TRUE)

  noise <- noise %>% mutate(n_samples_affected = unname(samples_touched[species]))
  write_tsv(noise, noise_out)

  summary <- tibble(
    sample = sample_ids,
    removed_before_renormalisation = unname(removed_total),
    renormalisation_factor = unname(factor)
  )

  if (!quiet) {
    message(sprintf("Positive controls: %s", paste(strip_s_suffix(positive_cols), collapse = ", ")))
    message(sprintf("Noise species: %d. Largest ceiling: %s (%.5f%%).", nrow(noise), noise$species[1], noise$ceiling_abundance[1]))
    message(sprintf("Samples with any subtraction: %d of %d. Largest total removed from one sample: %.4f%%.",
                    sum(removed_total > 0), length(sample_cols), max(removed_total)))
    message("Wrote ", table_out)
    message("Wrote ", noise_out)
  }

  invisible(list(noise = noise, sample_summary = summary, table_file = table_out, noise_file = noise_out))
}
still_present <- metadata$sample_name_clean %in% MISLABELED_SAMPLES
if (any(still_present) && !all(metadata$sample_type[still_present] == "mislabeled")) {

}
metadata <- metadata %>% filter(!still_present)
decontamination <- decontaminate_metaphlan(ROOT, quiet = TRUE)

      country == "Israel" & monument_final == "Tel_Megiddo" & materials_plot == "others" ~ "Israel — others",
      country == "Israel" & monument_final == "Tel_Megiddo" & materials_plot == "rock/stone" ~ "Israel — rock/stone",
      country == "United States" & monument %in% c("Orpheus", "Soldier's National Monument") & materials_plot == "marble" ~ "United States — marble",
      country == "United States" & monument %in% c("Charging Bull", "Fearless Girl") & materials_plot == "metal" ~ "United States — metal",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(focal_group))
```

# Figure 1. Where Monumentome was sampled, and which samples the paper uses

This is the overview figure. It has three panels, each saved as its own PNG in `paper_output/Figure1/`. The map is the image you supplied. The two bar charts are the original sampling figure, reordered by sample size. Each bar chart carries its own material legend, so a panel can be placed alone.

## Panel A. Geographic map

Panel A is `paper_assets/Figure1A_map.png`, with the panel letter added. It is not drawn from coordinates. The source file is 784 by 616 pixels, so this panel will look soft in print until a higher-resolution export replaces it.

## Panel B. Original sampling structure

Panel B counts every sample in the metadata, one bar per `monument_final` label. Stack segments are material. Bars run from the largest sample size on the left to the smallest on the right. Underscores in the monument labels are printed as spaces. This panel is the full collection, before the species filter used later in the paper.

## Panel C. Five focal monument–material groups

Panel C counts only samples kept for analysis: at least 2 detected species, and only the five pre-specified monument–material groups. Each bar is one focal group, ordered by descending sample size. Groups tied at 15 samples stay in alphabetical order: Israel — others, then Israel — rock/stone. Each group name is on two lines: place on the first line and material on the second.

```{r figure1, fig.width=13.5, fig.height=16.4, out.width="100%"}

}
```

The combined figure is `paper_output/Figure1_overview.pdf` and `paper_output/Figure1_overview.png`. Saved panels are `paper_output/Figure1/Figure1A_map.png`, `paper_output/Figure1/Figure1B_original_sampling.png`, and `paper_output/Figure1/Figure1C_focal_groups.png`.

# Figure 2. Species profiles of the five focal monument–material groups

Panels A–D are the UMAP, species-accumulation curve, richness, and Shannon diversity from the analysis notebook. Panels E and F are the Jaccard NMDS and the pairwise Jaccard distances. Each of the six panels is saved as its own PNG in `paper_output/Figure2/`, and the panels that color points by group (A, B, E) carry their own legend.

Each group keeps the material color from Figure 1. Brazil - granite is pink, Israel - others is blue, Israel - rock/stone is green, United States - marble is dark yellow, and United States - metal is brown. Legend names use a plain hyphen so the group names render in the figure font.

## Panel A. Species-profile UMAP

Hellinger-transformed species abundances are embedded with UMAP, using the same seed and settings as the analysis notebook. Points and ellipses are colored by focal monument–material group.

## Panel B. Species accumulation

Random accumulation curves, with a band of one standard deviation across permutations. The x-axis is the number of samples.

## Panels C and D. Richness and Shannon diversity

Observed species richness and Shannon diversity for each retained focal sample. Boxes and points use the group color. The subtitle is the Kruskal–Wallis p-value. Group names are stacked, as in Figure 1, so the labels stay readable.

## Panel E. Jaccard NMDS

Non-metric multidimensional scaling of Jaccard distances among focal samples, using species presence or absence. Species detected in only one sample are omitted, because they push most pairwise distances to 1 and collapse the NMDS; a sample with no remaining species is omitted with them. The subtitle reports the number of samples, the NMDS stress, the PERMANOVA R², and the permutation p-value (999 permutations) for a difference among the five groups. A p-value of 0.001 is the smallest the test can return, so it is written as p < 0.001.

## Panel F. Median Jaccard distance

The boxplot of every sample pair is replaced by a heatmap of one triangle of the group-by-group matrix. The upper triangle is left blank so each pair is shown once. The diagonal is the median distance among samples inside a group. Every other filled cell is the median distance between samples from two different groups. The printed number is that median.

```{r figure2, fig.width=14, fig.height=16.5, out.width="100%"}
FIG2_DIR <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Figure2")
# Check panels carry their own legend. In the print page one shared legend sits under the
# six panels, so the panels themselves have none.
focal_legend_bottom <- if (is_print()) {
  list(theme(legend.position = "none"))
} else {
  list(
    guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE, title.position = "top", override.aes = list(size = 4, alpha = 1))),
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
  )
}

# One-row legend of the five focal groups, used by every print page that colors by group.
focal_group_legend <- function() {
  src <- ggplot(
    tibble(focal_group = factor(FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS, levels = FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS), x = 1, y = 1),
    aes(x, y, color = focal_group)
  ) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    scale_color_manual(values = FOCAL_GROUP_COLORS, labels = FOCAL_LEGEND_LABELS, name = "Focal group") +
    guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 1, override.aes = list(size = 2.4))) +
    theme_void(base_family = FIG_FONT) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = FIG_LEGEND_TITLE_SIZE),
      legend.text = element_text(size = FIG_LEGEND_TEXT_SIZE),
      legend.key.size = unit(0.3, "cm")
    )
  wrap_elements(full = cowplot::get_legend(src))
}

hellinger_matrix <- decostand(focal_species_matrix, method = "hellinger")

focal_umap <- uwot::umap(
  hellinger_matrix,
  n_neighbors = min(15L, nrow(hellinger_matrix) - 1L),

  metric = "euclidean",
  scale = FALSE,
  init = "spectral",
  n_threads = 1L,
  verbose = FALSE
)

accumulation_data <- bind_rows(lapply(FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS, function(group_name) {
  sample_ids <- focal_species_metadata %>%
    filter(focal_group == group_name) %>%
    pull(sample_name_clean)
  acc <- specaccum(focal_species_presence[sample_ids, , drop = FALSE], method = "random", permutations = RICHNESS_PERMUTATIONS)
  tibble(
    focal_group = group_name,
    n_samples = acc$sites,
    accumulated_richness = acc$richness,

  )
})) %>%

focal_beta <- jaccard_beta(

focal_permanova <- focal_beta$permanova

  labs(

    ),

bray_matrix <- as.matrix(focal_beta$dist)
pair_index <- which(upper.tri(bray_matrix), arr.ind = TRUE)
group_lookup <- setNames(as.integer(focal_species_metadata$focal_group), focal_species_metadata$sample_name_clean)
sample_1 <- rownames(bray_matrix)[pair_index[, 1]]
sample_2 <- colnames(bray_matrix)[pair_index[, 2]]
group_1 <- group_lookup[sample_1]
group_2 <- group_lookup[sample_2]

median_bray <- tibble(
  group_low = pmin(group_1, group_2),
  group_high = pmax(group_1, group_2),
  bray_curtis = bray_matrix[pair_index]
) %>%
  group_by(group_low, group_high) %>%
  summarise(median_distance = median(bray_curtis), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    x = factor(FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS[group_low], levels = FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS),
    y = factor(FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS[group_high], levels = FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS),
    label = sprintf("%.2f", median_distance)
  )

p_2f <- ggplot(median_bray, aes(x, y, fill = median_distance)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = gs(0.6)) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label, color = ifelse(median_distance > 0.85, "white", "grey10")),
    size = pt_to_mm(FIG_SMALL_TEXT_SIZE + by_mode(2, 0)),
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_color_identity() +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = focal_axis_labels(), drop = FALSE) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = focal_axis_labels(), limits = rev(FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS), drop = FALSE) +
  colorspace::scale_fill_continuous_sequential(
    palette = "Blues 3",
    rev = TRUE,
    limits = c(0, 1),
    name = "Median distance"
  ) +
  labs(tag = "F", title = "Median Jaccard distance", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  paper_theme_continuous() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(lineheight = 0.95),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = if (is_print()) c(0.80, 0.80) else "right"
  ) +
  coord_fixed()

fig2_files <- c(
  save_panel(p_2a, FIG2_DIR, "Figure2A_umap", width = 10, height = 8.5),
  save_panel(p_2b, FIG2_DIR, "Figure2B_species_accumulation", width = 10, height = 8.5),
  save_panel(p_2c, FIG2_DIR, "Figure2C_richness", width = 10, height = 7.5),
  save_panel(p_2d, FIG2_DIR, "Figure2D_shannon", width = 10, height = 7.5),
  save_panel(p_2e, FIG2_DIR, "Figure2E_jaccard_nmds", width = 10, height = 8.5),
  save_panel(p_2f, FIG2_DIR, "Figure2F_median_jaccard", width = 11.5, height = 10)
)

if (is_print()) {
  # Three panels per row keeps the page under 170 mm tall (Nature).
  fig2_heights <- c(2.75, 2.9, 0.35)
  # Five group names share a 2.4-inch panel, so their tick labels are 5.5 pt (Nature allows 5 to 7 pt).
  p_2c <- p_2c + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 5.5))
  p_2d <- p_2d + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 5.5))
  p_2f <- p_2f + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 5.5), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5.5))
  figure2 <- (
    (blk(p_2a) | blk(p_2b) | blk(p_2c)) /
    (blk(p_2d) | blk(p_2e) | blk(p_2f)) /
    focal_group_legend()
  ) + plot_layout(heights = fig2_heights)
  fig2_files <- save_page(figure2, OUTPUT_DIR, "Figure2_focal_groups", height = sum(fig2_heights))
}
knitr::include_graphics(fig2_files)
```

The combined figure is `paper_output/Figure2_focal_groups.pdf` and `paper_output/Figure2_focal_groups.png`. Saved panels are in `paper_output/Figure2/`: `Figure2A_umap.png`, `Figure2B_species_accumulation.png`, `Figure2C_richness.png`, `Figure2D_shannon.png`, `Figure2E_jaccard_nmds.png`, and `Figure2F_median_jaccard.png`.

# Figure 3. Who overlaps, and what the groups are made of

Panels A–C are presence/absence Venn diagrams for species, genus, and phylum. Panels D and E are the mean MetaPhlAn composition bars. The genus bar keeps the notebook rule: the top 10 genera inside each group, then the union of those lists, with everything else pooled as Other. The phylum bar shows every detected phylum.

The circle outlines and group names use the same five colors as Figures 1 and 2, so Brazil granite is pink in the Venn and pink in the earlier plots. The names are written on two lines, without the em dash, because that character was printing as `<U+2014>`. Each Venn is kept square so the ellipses are not stretched, and the row is only as tall as the diagrams. The shaded overlap regions stay on one light scale. An overlap belongs to more than one group, so filling it with a group color would mix five meanings in one patch. The number in each region is the count of taxa. The stacked bars use a separate color for each genus or phylum, because those colors identify taxa rather than groups.

```{r figure3, fig.width=16, fig.height=12.2, out.width="100%"}
FIG3_DIR <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Figure3")

focal_ids <- intersect(focal_sample_key$sample_name_clean, sample_cols)
rank_rows <- metaphlan_wide %>%
  bind_cols(parse_terminal_rank(metaphlan_wide$clade_name)) %>%
  filter(rank %in% c("phylum", "genus", "species"))

metaphlan_long <- rank_rows %>%
  select(rank, taxon, all_of(focal_ids)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(focal_ids), names_to = "sample_name_clean", values_to = "abundance") %>%
  mutate(abundance = as.numeric(abundance)) %>%
  filter(is.finite(abundance), abundance > 0)

make_taxon_sets <- function(rank_name) {
  sets <- metaphlan_long %>%
    filter(rank == rank_name, sample_name_clean %in% focal_sample_key$sample_name_clean) %>%
    inner_join(focal_sample_key %>% select(sample_name_clean, focal_group), by = "sample_name_clean") %>%
    distinct(focal_group, taxon) %>%
    group_by(focal_group) %>%
    summarise(taxa = list(sort(unique(taxon))), .groups = "drop")
  setNames(sets$taxa, as.character(sets$focal_group))[FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS]
}

# Group names are placed just outside the outline of their own ellipse, on the
# side that points away from the centre of the diagram, so no name sits on a line.
venn_name_positions <- function(sets, push = 55) {
  edges <- venn_setedge(process_data(Venn(sets)))
  centre <- c(500, 500)
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(sets), function(i) {
    e <- edges[edges$id == as.character(i), ]
    far <- which.max((e$X - centre[1])^2 + (e$Y - centre[2])^2)
    direction <- c(e$X[far] - centre[1], e$Y[far] - centre[2])
    direction <- direction / sqrt(sum(direction^2))
    tibble(
      x = e$X[far] + push * direction[1],
      y = e$Y[far] + push * direction[2],
      hjust = 0.5 - 0.5 * direction[1],
      vjust = 0.5 - 0.5 * direction[2],
      label = unname(focal_axis_labels()[FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS])[i],
      colour = unname(FOCAL_GROUP_COLORS[FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS])[i]
    )
  }))
}

plot_group_venn <- function(sets, title_text) {
  sets <- sets[FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS]
  name_positions <- venn_name_positions(sets)
  ggVennDiagram(
    sets,
    category.names = unname(focal_axis_labels()[FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS]),
    label = "count",
    label_alpha = 0,
    label_size = pt_to_mm(by_mode(14, 6)),
    set_size = 0,
    set_color = unname(FOCAL_GROUP_COLORS[FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS]),
    edge_size = gs(1.1)
  ) +
    geom_text(
      data = name_positions,
      aes(x = x, y = y, label = label, colour = I(colour), hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust),
      size = pt_to_mm(by_mode(15, 7)), fontface = "bold", lineheight = 0.95, inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#F7FBFF", "#DEEBF7", "#C6DBEF", "#9ECAE1", "#6BAED6")) +
    labs(title = title_text, fill = "Count") +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-190, 1190), ylim = c(-110, 1100), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
    venn_theme() +
    theme(legend.position = "right")
}

make_rank_matrix <- function(rank_name) {
  dat <- metaphlan_long %>%
    filter(rank == rank_name, sample_name_clean %in% focal_ids) %>%
    select(sample_name_clean, taxon, abundance) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = taxon, values_from = abundance, values_fill = 0) %>%
    tibble::column_to_rownames("sample_name_clean")
  as.matrix(dat[focal_ids, , drop = FALSE])
}

p_3a <- plot_group_venn(make_taxon_sets("species"), "Species overlap") + labs(tag = "A")
p_3b <- plot_group_venn(make_taxon_sets("genus"), "Genus overlap") + labs(tag = "B")
p_3c <- plot_group_venn(make_taxon_sets("phylum"), "Phylum overlap") + labs(tag = "C")

focal_genus_matrix <- make_rank_matrix("genus")
top10_by_group <- lapply(FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS, function(group_name) {
  ids <- focal_sample_key %>% filter(focal_group == group_name) %>% pull(sample_name_clean)
  ids <- intersect(ids, rownames(focal_genus_matrix))
  group_means <- colMeans(focal_genus_matrix[ids, , drop = FALSE])
  names(sort(group_means, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(10L, length(group_means)))]
})
genus_set <- unique(unlist(top10_by_group))
set.seed(RANDOM_SEED)
genus_colors <- c(
  setNames(Polychrome::createPalette(length(genus_set), seedcolors = pals::glasbey()), genus_set),
  Other = "grey70"
)

genus_composition <- bind_rows(lapply(FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS, function(group_name) {
  ids <- intersect(
    focal_sample_key %>% filter(focal_group == group_name) %>% pull(sample_name_clean),
    rownames(focal_genus_matrix)
  )
  means <- colMeans(focal_genus_matrix[ids, , drop = FALSE])
  tibble(
    focal_group = group_name,
    taxon = c(genus_set, "Other"),
    mean_abundance = c(means[genus_set], sum(means[setdiff(names(means), genus_set)]))
  )
})) %>%
  mutate(
    focal_group = factor(focal_group, levels = FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS),
    taxon = factor(taxon, levels = c(genus_set, "Other"))
  )

p_3d <- ggplot(genus_composition, aes(focal_group, mean_abundance, fill = taxon)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = genus_colors, drop = FALSE, name = "Genus") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = focal_axis_labels()) +
  labs(
    tag = "D",
    title = "Mean genus composition",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean MetaPhlAn relative abundance (%)"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = by_mode(2, 1), byrow = FALSE)) +
  paper_theme_upright() +
  theme(
    legend.text = element_text(size = by_mode(12, 5.5), face = "italic"),
    legend.key.size = unit(by_mode(0.5, 0.24), "cm")
  )

focal_phylum_matrix <- make_rank_matrix("phylum")
phylum_set <- names(sort(colSums(focal_phylum_matrix), decreasing = TRUE))
set.seed(RANDOM_SEED)
phylum_colors <- setNames(
  Polychrome::createPalette(length(phylum_set), seedcolors = c("#5A5156", "#E4E1E3", "#F6222E")),
  phylum_set
)

phylum_composition <- bind_rows(lapply(FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS, function(group_name) {
  ids <- intersect(
    focal_sample_key %>% filter(focal_group == group_name) %>% pull(sample_name_clean),
    rownames(focal_phylum_matrix)
  )
  means <- colMeans(focal_phylum_matrix[ids, , drop = FALSE])
  tibble(focal_group = group_name, taxon = phylum_set, mean_abundance = means[phylum_set])
})) %>%
  mutate(
    focal_group = factor(focal_group, levels = FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS),
    taxon = factor(taxon, levels = phylum_set)
  )

p_3e <- ggplot(phylum_composition, aes(focal_group, mean_abundance, fill = taxon)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = phylum_colors, drop = FALSE, name = "Phylum") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = focal_axis_labels()) +
  labs(
    tag = "E",
    title = "Mean phylum composition",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean MetaPhlAn relative abundance (%)"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = by_mode(1, 2))) +
  paper_theme_upright() +
  theme(
    legend.text = element_text(size = by_mode(12, 5.5), face = "italic"),
    legend.key.size = unit(by_mode(0.5, 0.26), "cm")
  )

fig3_files <- c(
  save_panel(p_3a, FIG3_DIR, "Figure3A_species_venn", width = 10.5, height = 9),
  save_panel(p_3b, FIG3_DIR, "Figure3B_genus_venn", width = 10.5, height = 9),
  save_panel(p_3c, FIG3_DIR, "Figure3C_phylum_venn", width = 10.5, height = 9),
  save_panel(p_3d, FIG3_DIR, "Figure3D_genus_composition", width = 14, height = 10),
  save_panel(p_3e, FIG3_DIR, "Figure3E_phylum_composition", width = 12, height = 9)
)
if (is_print()) {
  fig3_heights <- c(3.1, 4.3, 2.9)
  figure3 <- (
    (blk(p_3a) | blk(p_3b)) /
    ((blk(p_3c) | blk(p_3d)) + plot_layout(widths = c(3.3, 3.79))) /
    blk(p_3e)
  ) + plot_layout(heights = fig3_heights)
  fig3_files <- save_page(figure3, OUTPUT_DIR, "Figure3_overlap_composition", height = sum(fig3_heights))
}
knitr::include_graphics(fig3_files)
```

The combined figure is `paper_output/Figure3_overlap_composition.pdf` and `paper_output/Figure3_overlap_composition.png`. Saved panels are in `paper_output/Figure3/`: `Figure3A_species_venn.png`, `Figure3B_genus_venn.png`, `Figure3C_phylum_venn.png`, `Figure3D_genus_composition.png`, and `Figure3E_phylum_composition.png`.

# Figure 4. PAIS-NN ecosystems of the insertion sequences

A is the stacked ecosystem assignment for each sample with at least 200 IS, from `input/PAIS_NN_results_min200IS_UPDATE.xlsx`. Each bar is one sample, grouped by focal group and ordered by its largest ecosystem, and the colored strip under the bars is the focal group. Ecosystems that never reach 10% of any sample are pooled into one grey class, except Marine, which is sixth by mean proportion and is kept as its own class. B to G are the six ecosystems with the highest mean proportion: one boxplot per focal group, with a Kruskal-Wallis test and pairwise Mann-Whitney tests (BH-adjusted). The three Tel Megiddo `control` swabs are kept, as in the earlier figures.

```{r figure4, fig.width=14, fig.height=16, out.width="100%"}
FIG4_DIR <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Figure4")
PAIS_FILE <- file.path(ROOT, "input", "PAIS_NN_results_min200IS_UPDATE.xlsx")
PAIS_SHOW_MIN <- 0.10
K <- FIG_BASE_SIZE / 7
pais_result <- local({
  pais <- readxl::read_excel(PAIS_FILE)
  names(pais) <- str_replace_all(names(pais), "PAIS-NN", "PAISNN")
  fg_lookup <- setNames(FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS, str_replace(FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS, "\\s+\\W+\\s+", " "))
  pais <- pais %>%
    mutate(
      focal_group = factor(unname(fg_lookup[FocalGroup_Sample]), levels = FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS)
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(focal_group)) %>%
    select(Sample, focal_group, Ecosystem_PAISNN, Proportion_PAISNN) %>%
    complete(nesting(Sample, focal_group), Ecosystem_PAISNN, fill = list(Proportion_PAISNN = 0))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(pais$focal_group), all(abs(tapply(pais$Proportion_PAISNN, pais$Sample, sum) - 1) < 1e-6))

  eco_max <- tapply(pais$Proportion_PAISNN, pais$Ecosystem_PAISNN, max)
  eco_mean <- tapply(pais$Proportion_PAISNN, pais$Ecosystem_PAISNN, mean)
  eco_shown <- names(sort(eco_mean[eco_max >= PAIS_SHOW_MIN], decreasing = TRUE))
  if (!"Marine" %in% eco_shown) {
    eco_shown <- names(sort(eco_mean[c(eco_shown, "Marine")], decreasing = TRUE))
  }
  OTHER_LABEL <- sprintf("Other (%d ecosystems)", length(setdiff(names(eco_max), eco_shown)))
  eco_levels <- c(eco_shown, OTHER_LABEL)
  ECO_COLORS <- setNames(
    c(c("#332288", "#88CCEE", "#44AA99", "#117733", "#DDCC77", "#CC6677", "#AA4499", "#882255")[seq_along(eco_shown)], "grey75"),
    eco_levels
  )

  pais_plot <- pais %>%
    mutate(ecosystem = factor(if_else(Ecosystem_PAISNN %in% eco_shown, Ecosystem_PAISNN, OTHER_LABEL), levels = eco_levels)) %>%
    group_by(Sample, focal_group, ecosystem) %>%
    summarise(proportion = sum(Proportion_PAISNN), .groups = "drop")

  sample_order <- pais_plot %>%
    group_by(Sample) %>%
    slice_max(proportion, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(focal_group, ecosystem, desc(proportion)) %>%
    mutate(x = row_number())
  pais_bar <- pais_plot %>% left_join(select(sample_order, Sample, x), by = "Sample")
  strip_df <- sample_order %>% mutate(strip_color = unname(FOCAL_GROUP_COLORS[as.character(focal_group)]))
  p_a <- ggplot(pais_bar, aes(x, proportion, fill = ecosystem)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.9) +
    geom_tile(data = strip_df, aes(x = x, y = -0.035, fill = NULL, colour = NULL), fill = strip_df$strip_color, height = 0.045, width = 0.9, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = ECO_COLORS, name = "PAIS-NN ecosystem", drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), labels = function(v) paste0(round(100 * v), "%"), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1), clip = "off") +
    labs(tag = "A", title = "Ecosystem of origin of the IS (PAIS-NN)", x = "Samples, grouped by focal group", y = "Proportion of IS (%)") +
    paper_theme_continuous() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 12 * K)),
      legend.position = "right", legend.key.size = unit(0.3 * K, "cm")
    )

  box_ecos <- names(sort(eco_mean, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(6L, length(eco_mean)))]
  eco_tags <- LETTERS[seq_along(box_ecos) + 1L]
  group_scale_color <- scale_color_manual(values = FOCAL_GROUP_COLORS, labels = FOCAL_LEGEND_LABELS, drop = FALSE, name = "Focal group")
  group_scale_fill <- scale_fill_manual(values = FOCAL_GROUP_COLORS, labels = FOCAL_LEGEND_LABELS, drop = FALSE, name = "Focal group")

  box_plots <- vector("list", length(box_ecos))
  names(box_plots) <- box_ecos
  pairwise_list <- vector("list", length(box_ecos))
  names(pairwise_list) <- box_ecos
  kw_p <- setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(box_ecos)), box_ecos)
  for (i in seq_along(box_ecos)) {
    eco <- box_ecos[[i]]
    dat <- pais %>%
      filter(Ecosystem_PAISNN == eco) %>%
      mutate(pct = 100 * Proportion_PAISNN)
    kw <- kruskal.test(pct ~ focal_group, data = dat)
    pw <- pairwise_mannwhitney(dat$pct, dat$focal_group)
    kw_p[[eco]] <- kw$p.value
    pairwise_list[[eco]] <- pw
    br <- mw_bracket_data(dat$pct, dat$focal_group, pw)
    p_box <- ggplot(dat, aes(focal_group, pct, color = focal_group, fill = focal_group)) +
      geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.35) +
      geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = gs(2.2), alpha = 0.85, show.legend = FALSE) +
      group_scale_color + group_scale_fill +
      scale_x_discrete(labels = FOCAL_AXIS_LABELS_PRINT) +
      labs(
        tag = eco_tags[[i]],
        title = eco,
        subtitle = mw_kw_subtitle(kw$p.value, pw),
        x = NULL,
        y = "Proportion of IS (%)"
      ) +
      paper_theme_upright() +
      theme(
        legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = by_mode(11, 5.5), lineheight = 0.9),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = by_mode(11, 5.5), lineheight = 0.95)
      )
    if (nrow(br)) {
      p_box <- p_box +
        ggpubr::geom_bracket(
          aes(xmin = group1, xmax = group2, y.position = y.position, label = label),
          data = br,
          inherit.aes = FALSE,
          tip.length = 0.02,
          step.increase = 0,
          size = gs(0.4),
          label.size = pt_to_mm(by_mode(10, 5)),
          family = FIG_FONT,
          vjust = -0.15
        ) +
        coord_cartesian(
          ylim = {
            yr <- range(dat$pct, na.rm = TRUE)
            pad <- diff(yr)
            if (!is.finite(pad) || pad <= 0) pad <- max(abs(yr), 1)
            c(yr[[1]] - 0.04 * pad, max(br$y.position) + 0.10 * pad)
          },
          clip = "off"
        )
    }
    box_plots[[i]] <- p_box
  }

  group_legend_src <- ggplot(
    tibble(focal_group = factor(FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS, levels = FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS), x = 1, y = 1),
    aes(x, y, color = focal_group)
  ) +
    geom_point(size = gs(6)) +
    group_scale_color +
    guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 1, override.aes = list(size = gs(5.5)))) +
    theme_void(base_family = FIG_FONT) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = FIG_LEGEND_TITLE_SIZE),
      legend.text = element_text(size = FIG_LEGEND_TEXT_SIZE),
      legend.key.size = unit(0.3 * K, "cm")
    )
  focal_legend <- blk(cowplot::get_legend(group_legend_src))

  pais_page_heights <- c(2.35, 2.85, 2.85, 0.35)
  figure_pais <- (
    blk(p_a) /
      (blk(box_plots[[1]]) | blk(box_plots[[2]]) | blk(box_plots[[3]])) /
      (blk(box_plots[[4]]) | blk(box_plots[[5]]) | blk(box_plots[[6]])) /
      focal_legend
  ) + plot_layout(heights = pais_page_heights)

  eco_file <- function(eco) {
    paste0("Figure4", LETTERS[match(eco, box_ecos) + 1], "_", str_replace_all(tolower(eco), "[^a-z0-9]+", "_"))
  }
  if (!is_print()) {
    pais_files <- c(
      save_panel(p_a, FIG4_DIR, "Figure4A_pais_nn_ecosystems", width = 4.09 * K + 1.2, height = 3.2 * K),
      unlist(lapply(seq_along(box_ecos), function(i) {
        save_panel(box_plots[[i]], FIG4_DIR, eco_file(box_ecos[[i]]), width = 3.2 * K, height = 3.8 * K)
      }))
    )
  } else {
    pais_files <- save_page(figure_pais, OUTPUT_DIR, "Figure4_pais_nn", height = sum(pais_page_heights))
  }

  list(
    files = pais_files,
    n_pais_samples = n_distinct(pais$Sample),
    box_ecos = box_ecos,
    kw_p = kw_p,
    pairwise = pairwise_list
  )
})
knitr::include_graphics(pais_result$files)
```

A uses `r pais_result$n_pais_samples` samples with at least 200 IS. B to G are `r paste(pais_result$box_ecos, collapse = ", ")`. Each subtitle is the Kruskal-Wallis p-value across the five focal groups. Square brackets mark pairwise Mann-Whitney comparisons that remain below 0.05 after BH adjustment, with that adjusted p-value on the bracket.

The combined figure is `paper_output/Figure4_pais_nn.pdf` and `paper_output/Figure4_pais_nn.png`. Panels A to G are also in `paper_output/Figure4/`.

# Figure 5. Human-derived reads, and Charging Bull versus Fearless Girl

The figure has six panels. Panel A is the human-read percentage removed during host filtering, one box per original monument inside the focal groups, on the same retained samples as the later ecology (at least 2 detected species). Collapsed site codes are not used here, so Charging Bull and Fearless Girl are two separate boxes instead of one pooled NYC box. Panel B is species richness against that human-read percentage for all 112 focal swabs. Points use the focal-group colors. The black line is the linear fit, and the label gives its intercept, slope, R², and P. Panels C–F stay inside Charging Bull and Fearless Girl. C is the number of samples at each swabbed location. D is the human-derived DNA removed at locations sampled at least twice; the single Unknown swab stays in C and is left out of D. E is one panel with three Venn diagrams together: species, genera, and phyla shared by the two monuments, using the MetaPhlAn ranks as reported. F is the core-species heatmap: the union of species present in at least 75% of Charging Bull samples or 75% of Fearless Girl samples. The same two colors mark the monuments wherever a monument is colored: Charging Bull vermillion, Fearless Girl purple. Panel A is not colored by monument, because it compares six monuments at once. A–E fit one 170 mm page; F is a second page.

```{r figure5, fig.width=16, fig.height=36, out.width="100%"}
FIG5_DIR <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Figure5")

human_by_monument <- focal_sample_key %>%

      monument_ind,

        "Tel Megiddo",
        "Orpheus",
        "Soldier's National Monument",
        "Charging Bull",
        "Fearless Girl"
      ))
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(monument_ind))

human_kw <- kruskal.test(human_read_percent ~ monument_ind, data = human_by_monument)

p_4a <- ggplot(human_by_monument, aes(monument_ind, human_read_percent)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.62, fill = "white") +

    tag = "A",

  ) +
  # Extra room on the left so the first angled label is not cut off.

make_pair_sets <- function(rank_name) {
  sets <- cbfg_long %>%
    filter(rank == rank_name) %>%
    distinct(monument, taxon) %>%
    group_by(monument) %>%
    summarise(taxa = list(sort(unique(taxon))), .groups = "drop")
  setNames(sets$taxa, as.character(sets$monument))[c("Fearless Girl", "Charging Bull")]
}

plot_pair_venn <- function(sets, title_text) {
  sets <- sets[c("Charging Bull", "Fearless Girl")]
  ggVennDiagram(
    sets,
    category.names = c("", ""),
    label = "count",
    label_alpha = 0,
    label_size = pt_to_mm(by_mode(17, 6.5)),
    set_size = 0,
    set_color = unname(MONUMENT_PAIR_COLORS[c("Charging Bull", "Fearless Girl")]),
    edge_size = gs(1.15)
  ) +
    geom_text(
      data = data.frame(x = 0, y = -4.7, label = "Charging Bull"),
      aes(x, y, label = label),
      colour = unname(MONUMENT_PAIR_COLORS["Charging Bull"]),
      hjust = 0.5, size = pt_to_mm(by_mode(17, 7)), fontface = "bold", inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    geom_text(
      data = data.frame(x = 0, y = 8.55, label = "Fearless Girl"),
      aes(x, y, label = label),
      colour = unname(MONUMENT_PAIR_COLORS["Fearless Girl"]),
      hjust = 0.5, size = pt_to_mm(by_mode(17, 7)), fontface = "bold", inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#F7FBFF", "#DEEBF7", "#C6DBEF", "#9ECAE1", "#6BAED6")) +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-4.4, 4.4), ylim = c(-5.5, 9.5), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title_text) +
    venn_theme() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
}

p_4e_species <- plot_pair_venn(make_pair_sets("species"), "Species shared") + labs(tag = "E")

# Panel E is three Venn diagrams in one image.

fig4_taxa <- str_remove(str_extract(species_rows$clade_name, "[^|]+$"), "^s__")

fig4_species_cbfg <- fig4_species_all[cbfg_ids, , drop = FALSE]
monument_prevalence <- bind_rows(lapply(c("Charging Bull", "Fearless Girl"), function(mon) {
  ids <- cbfg_meta %>% filter(monument == mon) %>% pull(sample_name_clean)
  mat <- fig4_species_cbfg[ids, , drop = FALSE]
  tibble(monument = mon, taxon = colnames(mat), prevalence = colMeans(mat > 0))
}))
cb_core <- monument_prevalence %>% filter(monument == "Charging Bull", prevalence >= CORE_THRESHOLD) %>% pull(taxon)
fg_core <- monument_prevalence %>% filter(monument == "Fearless Girl", prevalence >= CORE_THRESHOLD) %>% pull(taxon)
core_order <- c(intersect(cb_core, fg_core), setdiff(fg_core, cb_core), setdiff(cb_core, fg_core))
us_ids <- focal_sample_key %>%
  filter(focal_group == FOCAL_GROUP_LEVELS[5]) %>%
  pull(sample_name_clean)
us_prevalence <- colMeans(fig4_species_all[us_ids, , drop = FALSE] > 0)
us_metal_core <- names(us_prevalence)[us_prevalence >= CORE_THRESHOLD]
heatmap_positions <- c("FG_Bottom", "FG_Top", "Butt", "Face", "Untouched_Bottom")
position_prevalence <- bind_rows(lapply(heatmap_positions, function(pos) {
  ids <- cbfg_meta %>% filter(swab_position == pos) %>% pull(sample_name_clean)
  mat <- fig4_species_cbfg[ids, core_order, drop = FALSE]
  tibble(taxon = core_order, display_group = pos, prevalence = colMeans(mat > 0))
}))
core_heatmap_data <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    taxon = core_order,
    display_group = "US metal",
    prevalence = unname(us_prevalence[core_order])
  ),
  position_prevalence
) %>%
  mutate(
    block = case_when(
      display_group == "US metal" ~ "Pooled",
      display_group %in% c("FG_Bottom", "FG_Top") ~ "Fearless Girl",

    ),
    display_group = factor(
      display_group,

    ),

core_axis_labels <- setNames(

  ),

)
n_core_taxa <- length(core_order)
fig4_core <- list(
  n_core = n_core_taxa,
  n_both = length(intersect(cb_core, fg_core)),
  n_cb_only = length(setdiff(cb_core, fg_core)),
  n_fg_only = length(setdiff(fg_core, cb_core)),
  n_starred = sum(core_order %in% us_metal_core)
)

p_4f <- ggplot(core_heatmap_data, aes(display_group, taxon, fill = 100 * prevalence)) +

    x = NULL,

  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = FIG_BASE_SIZE, base_family = FIG_FONT) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = FIG_TITLE_SIZE, margin = margin(t = 10 * FIG_BASE_SIZE / 15, b = 6 * FIG_BASE_SIZE / 15)),
    plot.title.position = "plot",

    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = FIG_BASE_SIZE, colour = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = by_mode(14, FIG_BASE_SIZE), colour = "black", face = "italic"),

fig4_files <- c(
  save_panel(p_4a, FIG5_DIR, "Figure5A_human_reads_by_monument", width = 12, height = 8.5),
  save_panel(p_4b, FIG5_DIR, "Figure5B_richness_vs_human_reads", width = 11, height = 9),

  # A-E on one page, at most 170 mm tall (Nature). F is a second page.
  fig4_heights <- c(2.3, 2.3, 2.05)
  figure5 <- (
    (blk(p_4a) | blk(p_4b)) /

  ) + plot_layout(heights = fig4_heights)
```
